from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Core Logic: Bernoulli's Insight"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bernoulli treated the sliding particle as a light beam.",
            "The refractive index changes at every level of depth.",
            "Use the formula sin theta over velocity equals constant.",
            "As velocity increases, the angle must also increase.",
            "This optical analogy reveals the shape of quickest descent."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Helper for Cycloid
        # x = R(t - sin t), y = R(1 - cos t). We'll flip y for descent.
        R = 0.8
        def cycloid_func(t):
            # Shifted to fit in the grid area A1-F6
            # Start at A1 (0.5, 2.2)
            # End roughly near E5
            start_x = self.grid["A1"][0]
            start_y = self.grid["A1"][1]
            return np.array([
                start_x + R * (t - np.sin(t)),
                start_y - R * (1 - np.cos(t)),
                0
            ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Descent curve (Cycloid)
        curve = ParametricFunction(cycloid_func, t_range=[0, np.pi], color=BLUE)
        # Overlay "light path" from Section 3 (representing discretized layers)
        num_layers = 5
        t_vals = np.linspace(0, np.pi, num_layers + 1)
        light_path_pts = [cycloid_func(t) for t in t_vals]
        light_path = VGroup(*[
            Line(light_path_pts[i], light_path_pts[i+1], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            for i in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=2)
        self.play(Create(light_path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Horizontal bands for refractive index
        bands = VGroup()
        colors = [BLUE_E, BLUE_D, BLUE_C, BLUE_B, BLUE_A]
        for i in range(5):
            band_y = self.grid["A1"][1] - i * 0.8
            rect = Rectangle(width=6, height=0.8, fill_opacity=0.2, fill_color=colors[i], stroke_width=0)
            rect.move_to(np.array([self.grid["C3"][0], band_y - 0.4, 0]))
            bands.add(rect)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(bands), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Formula: sin(theta)/v = constant
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant}", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Value tracker for the point on the curve
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        def get_point():
            return cycloid_func(t_tracker.get_value())
        
        def get_tangent_line():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            # derivative: dx/dt = R(1-cos t), dy/dt = -R(sin t)
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            angle = np.arctan2(dy, dx)
            # Line centered at p
            line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=RED).scale(0.5).rotate(angle).move_to(p)
            return line

        def get_theta_visuals():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            # theta is the angle from the VERTICAL (normal to layers)
            # The velocity vector is along the tangent.
            # Angle of tangent with horizontal: arctan2(dy, dx)
            # Since y is downward, dy is negative. 
            # theta is angle with the negative y-axis (vertical downward).
            # Tangent vector: (dx, dy)
            # Vertical downward vector: (0, -1)
            # dot product: |v| * 1 * cos(alpha) = dy * (-1) = -dy
            # but theta in Snell's law is usually angle with normal.
            # Here layers are horizontal, normal is vertical.
            
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            
            tangent_vec = np.array([dx, dy, 0])
            tangent_vec /= np.linalg.norm(tangent_vec)
            
            normal_vec = np.array([0, 1, 0]) # Vertical UP for reference
            
            # Draw vertical dashed line
            v_line = DashedLine(p + UP*0.5, p + DOWN*0.5, color=GREY)
            
            # Angle arc
            # The angle between tangent and vertical:
            # dy/dx = -sin(t)/(1-cos(t)) = -2sin(t/2)cos(t/2) / (2sin^2(t/2)) = -cot(t/2)
            # angle with horizontal = arctan(-cot(t/2)) = - (pi/2 - t/2)
            # angle theta (with vertical) = t/2
            
            arc = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=t/2, arc_center=p, color=WHITE)
            label = MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=20).next_to(arc, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            
            # Velocity vector
            v_arrow = Arrow(p, p + tangent_vec * 0.8, buff=0, color=ORANGE)
            v_label = MathTex("v", font_size=20, color=ORANGE).next_to(v_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.05)
            
            return VGroup(v_line, arc, label, v_arrow, v_label)

        # Using add_updater for the point and visuals
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_point()))
        
        tangent = always_redraw(get_tangent_line)
        theta_stuff = always_redraw(get_theta_visuals)
        
        self.add(dot, tangent, theta_stuff)
        
        # Animate the point moving
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # Scale formula for emphasis
        self.play(formula.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(GOLD), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight curve
        self.play(curve.animate.set_color("#FF00FF").set_stroke(width=6))
        self.wait(2)
